parts.credit_requirement: Calculate cooling rate over a supplied interval: temperature change/time (1), value and unit (1).

parts.credit_requirement: State a thermometer measures the temperature (1).

parts.credit_requirement: Plan insulation comparison: same vessel/water volume (1), same starting temperature (1), vary only insulation material (1), record temperature at fixed times (1), repeat/control ambient conditions (1), compare cooling curves for a conclusion (1).

answer_requirements: Original realistic data/observations and an appropriate labelled apparatus or graph visual
Worked calculations, units and numerical tolerance where relevant
Separate plotting/curve/read-off criteria rather than an undifferentiated graph mark
For six-mark planning: setup, controls, measurements and conclusion; state alternatives and any thresholds
For tests: reagent, initial observation, excess-reagent behaviour and final solution colour where applicable
Describe activities on paper; do not imply unsupervised hazardous experiments

stimulus_specification.context: Equal 100 cm³ water portions start at 80 °C in identical vessels; compare insulation at room temperature 22 °C.
apparatus_labels: thermometer bulb immersed but not touching vessel
stimulus_specification.safety: Teacher supplies hot water; heatproof mat and burn precautions.
stimulus_specification.data_provenance: Original synthetic teaching data; not experimental measurements or official paper data.

performance_tasks.answer_tolerance_policy: Use stated tolerances for visual readings; exact arithmetic uses unrounded values. Accept correct follow-through from an allowed reading, without double penalising it.

ao_mix_note: The syllabus states its AO weights as a share of MARKS, so planned_ao_mix_by_marks is the one that answers "does this resource match the exam". It values each card at the tariff of the question it models, split across the AOs the card declares, and values each performance task at the marks of the paper part it models. The count-based mix below is reported only because it is what a reader expects to see; do not balance against it. AO shares by ITEM COUNT: Every objective needs one recall anchor, so AO1 has a structural floor of about 45% in this topic (15 objectives against 33 slots) and cannot reach the None% target by count however many other cards are added - padding the bank to chase it makes the resource worse. The framework already measures the AO4 share in practice time rather than by count for the same reason. Treat AO1 above target as expected, and AO2/AO3/AO4 below target as the thing worth fixing.
